MY AUDIT!

- I feel like the references are not being used fully. Most of the imagery seems to take place on one part of the same ship. I do see some subtle, nuanced elements that may or may not be on this particular cruise ship, but a lot of the defining features of the ship are just not found in the images being generated now. 
- There's probably a lot of conflicting information throughout the system about how many people, if any, to put in these images. The overall overriding rule should be that group action is the priority. While theme details and ship details are important, the theme should be group-driven. The imagery should always have four to six, even ten, people involved in some kind of activity that speaks to the theme of the cruise. This thought process has changed over time based off of the quality of the image generation by the models, but at this point I believe that is less of an issue. 
- There is an overabundance of people sitting at tables, eating and drinking, or staring over a rail. This is fine for 10% of the imagery, but not 90% as I'm saying now. This really points out the need for diversification of the images, specifically diversity in ethnicity and in age. Right now I see the same thirty-something year old white lady and her husband in pretty much every image. 
- We may need to somewhat embellish the activity of the theme cruise, even if it's more than what we might actually see in real life. The way the images are now seems a little bit mundane. Even though they might be, for all intents and purposes, correctly portraying the theme, the images are still coming across as sort of dull and not much activity one way or the other. 
- At first, I was skeptical about embellishment because I didn't want to necessarily false sell anything or over-hype anything, but I'm starting to rethink that logic because the whole idea is to attract the guest's attention, at least when we're dealing with ads. The landing page will sort of calibrate the user's expectations that everything is sort of a potential and not necessarily a given. The landing page will sort of calibrate the user's expectations that everything is sort of a potential and not necessarily a given. 
- We still have some of the "watercolor" images drifting into the hero shots. I am pretty certain we're not going to use any of these, but it may be good to keep them in a specifically unique section where they could be used as alternative images in a specific campaign. But they should not be in the main selected photos that the orchestrator chooses from. 
- I would like to revisit the ideas that we explored earlier of using different sepia tones or black and white or some kind of filters on some of these images, just to give them different looks.
